chunks: And by his chain, that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was visited by a man who said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin! A thief entered upon my wife and stole her ornaments.'
So Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, if he had entered upon a son of Safiyyah, he would not have been pleased with that until he had covered him with the sword.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.ابْنُ صَفِيَّةَ: Son of Safiyyah (a title often referring to the Prophet Muhammad or the Imams, indicating noble lineage)
key_terms.يَعُمَّهُ بِالسَّيْفِ: He covered him with the sword (meaning to kill him)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about a thief stealing from the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the concept of *al-dar’* (right of self-defense) and the elevated status of the Ahl al-Bayt, using the phrase 'son of Safiyyah' to refer to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny). It illustrates that while theft from ordinary individuals is a crime, the violation of the sanctity of the Imams' homes was considered a grave affront to their honor, warranting immediate and decisive retribution. This narrative underscores the practical application of justice and the distinct reverence accorded to the Prophet's lineage in Shia jurisprudence.
